schema_purpose: Corrected hierarchy for Punjab Professional Tax classification and rate implementation.

source.title: Punjab Professional Tax - Second Schedule rate rules
source.source_scope_note: This rule set reproduces the statutory classifications and annual rates appearing in the user-provided PDF. Machine fields normalize the legal text for implementation. Tertiary classifications are an analytical/entity-type allocation layer derived only from distinct types expressly enumerated inside the same statutory entry; they do not create new tax rates.
amendment_notes_visible_in_pdf: Second Schedule substituted by the Punjab Finance Act 2019 (XV of 2019), as noted in the PDF footnote.
Entry 3 substituted by the Punjab Finance Act 2021 (XIX of 2021), as noted in the PDF footnote.
In entry 6(vii)(d), 'Motor Vehicle' was substituted for 'Motor Car' by the Punjab Finance Act 2021 (XIX of 2021).
Entry 11 was inserted by the Punjab Finance Act 2021 (XIX of 2021).
source.code_note: subclassification_code follows the numbering hierarchy printed in the Second Schedule. rule_id is a stable machine-friendly key. tertiary_code is an implementation code for a finer entity-type allocation within an existing statutory subclassification and is not a statutory schedule number.

hierarchy_contract.category: The numbered main class of persons in the Second Schedule (e.g. entry 6: persons engaged in various professions and services).
hierarchy_contract.subclassification: A meaningful statutory sub-class/slab beneath a category. The code is an identifier; the wording is the class label. Example: code 1(i), label Paid-up capital up to Rs 5 million.
hierarchy_contract.tertiary_classification: A genuine further split below a category/subclassification. It may be (a) a numbered statutory child such as 6(vii)(e)(i) location, or (b) a source-enumerated entity type such as Jeweler under 6(x). If no further split exists, leave it null/empty.
hierarchy_contract.criteria: Conditions used to determine applicability (capital, employees, value, AC facility, etc.). Criteria must never be copied into tertiary_classification merely to fill the field.
hierarchy_contract.code_semantics: Codes such as 1(i) and 6(vii)(e) are identifiers/paths, not class names. Never display a code itself as the classification wording.
hierarchy_contract.nullable_levels: Do not fabricate subclassifications or tertiary classifications. Entries 7-11 have no separate numbered statutory subclass in the source; their grouped entity types can be represented by category-level analytic tertiary dimensions.
hierarchy_contract.multiple_tertiary_dimensions: A subclass can legitimately have more than one tertiary dimension. Example: 6(v) can have profession_type (Management Consultant, Architect, etc.) and statutory location_scope (Metro/Municipal vs Others). Store these as separate dimensions, not as one overwritten field.

do_not_do: Do not set tertiary_classification equal to subclassification when no further split exists.
Do not turn criteria such as “Paid-up capital up to Rs 5 million” into a tertiary class when it is already the subclassification.
Do not treat an entry code such as 1(i) as a class label.
Do not merge entity-type tertiary dimensions with statutory location tertiary dimensions; both may coexist.
Do not invent a tertiary type solely because a field is required by the application UI.
Do not use recovery amount to infer an unrelated entity type.

implementation_rules.tertiary_null_rule: If no genuine further split exists or the finer type cannot be identified reliably, tertiary fields must be null/empty; never copy the subclassification into tertiary.
implementation_rules.multi_year_recovery: After category/rule evidence is established, recovery may be checked as annual_rate_pkr multiplied by an exact positive whole number of years. Do not invent sums, percentages, or cross-category formulas to force a match.
